content:
customer-alice: Hey support — since yesterday at ~10:00 UTC our prod service started getting intermittent 502 and 403 errors when calling Redwood over our PrivateLink endpoint. Errors look like TLS handshake resets and occasional DNS resolving to public IP. No config changes on our side. Can you help?

marta-support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste a short repro (curl -v) and a dig + traceroute output for the Redwood hostname? Also the VPC Endpoint ID and which subnets it's in.

customer-alice: Thanks. Repro from one app node (private subnet):
```
$ curl -v https://api.redwood-inference.example.com/v1/ping --max-time 10
* Connected to api.redwood-inference.example.com (34.210.11.9) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake has read 0 bytes and written 300 bytes
* recv failed (104: Connection reset by peer)
* Closing connection 0
curl: (56) recv failed (104: Connection reset by peer)
```

Dig/traceroute: 
```
$ dig +short api.redwood-inference.example.com
34.210.11.9
$ traceroute api.redwood-inference.example.com
1  ip-10-0-1-1.ec2.internal (10.0.1.1) ...
...
6  34.210.11.9 (34.210.11.9)  2.1 ms  2.0 ms  2.1 ms
```

Endpoint: vpce-0abc12345 in subnets 10.0.1.0/24,10.0.2.0/24. SG inbound allows 443 from our subnets. Route tables: private subnets default route -> nat-0e1f (0.0.0.0/0).

marta-support: Two quick things to confirm: 1) is Private DNS enabled/associated on the interface endpoint? 2) are your resolver rules forwarding the Redwood private DNS to the VPC endpoint resolver? Also, that traceroute resolving to a public IP (34.210...) suggests Private DNS might not be resolving to the ENI IP.

andrew-eng: +1. Also check that route table doesn't accidentally send outbound HTTPS to the NAT instead of the interface endpoint (interface endpoints are ENIs, but app traffic to the API hostname should go directly to endpoint via Private DNS mapping). If traffic goes to NAT it'll egress and use the EIP, which can cause auth/403 if you have IP allowlists.

customer-alice: We just confirmed Private DNS was NOT enabled on the endpoint (we created the VPCE via TF module that left it off). When we enable it, we expect DNS to resolve to 10.0.x.y ENI IPs. Any quick test we can run?

marta-support: Yes — from an app node, test with curl + --resolve to force the ENI IP once you have it:
```
# replace 10.0.1.23 with the endpoint ENI private IP
curl -v --resolve api.redwood-inference.example.com:443:10.0.1.23 https://api.redwood-inference.example.com/v1/ping
```
That isolates DNS. Also run: `dig api.redwood-inference.example.com @10.0.0.2` (your VPC resolver) to confirm it's returning the ENI IP.

customer-alice: Ran the tests. After enabling Private DNS, `dig` returns `10.0.1.23` (ENI). curl with --resolve to 10.0.1.23 shows successful TLS but intermittent 502s remain for some calls. Capture attached (tcpdump excerpt):
```
14:22:17.123 IP 10.0.1.45.43210 > 10.0.1.23.443: Flags [S], seq 12345, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 123 ecr 0], length 0
14:22:17.223 IP 10.0.1.23.443 > 10.0.1.45.43210: Flags [R] seq 0 win 0 length 0
# TLS record: server sends TLS alert (unknown_ca) then RST
```

andrew-eng: RSTs + TLS alert unknown_ca usually means SNI/certname mismatch or a TLS proxy in the path rejecting handshake. Is there any transparent TLS inspection/firewall in front of the endpoint ENIs (security appliances in the subnet or host-level iptables)?

customer-alice: We do have an outbound proxy in our VPC subnets for some AZs (iptables TPROXY intercept) but thought it was only for centralized logging. Could that rewrite or strip SNI?

marta-support: Yes — interception/proxy can strip SNI or present a different cert if it's performing TLS interception. That will make the client get unknown_ca from the server side (or vice versa). Check host-level iptables and any egress SG/NACLs that might redirect traffic via a proxy appliance. Also check your endpoint ENI SGs — make sure they allow inbound from the app SG and that there are no iptables PREROUTING REDIRECT rules.

customer-alice: Found iptables REDIRECT rule in /etc/rc.local on our app AMI for outbound 443 -> local proxy in some AZs. We removed it from one instance and retried — curl to ENI succeeded consistently on that node.

ops-lead: Good find. Two follow ups: 1) If some AZs still intercept TLS, that will explain intermittent behavior across AZs. Remove/whitelist PrivateLink ENI CIDRs in the proxy rules. 2) For the 403s earlier, confirm if your app was egressing via NAT prior to Private DNS — IP allowlist on Redwood may have blocked EIP; either add NAT EIP to allowlist or reconfigure to route to the endpoint.

marta-support: For completeness, here are repro and diagnostic commands we recommend you run cluster-wide: 
```
# capture TLS handshake details
sudo tcpdump -i any port 443 -w /tmp/redwood-tls.pcap
# check DNS from node
dig +short api.redwood-inference.example.com @169.254.169.123 # your resolver IP
# force ENI test
curl -v --resolve api.redwood-inference.example.com:443:10.0.1.23 https://api.redwood-inference.example.com/v1/ping
# verify conntrack / iptables rules
sudo iptables -t nat -L -n -v
```

customer-alice: We rolled out removal of the REDIRECT rules and enabled Private DNS on the endpoint. After that both TLS handshake errors and 502s stopped. We did have to add our NAT EIP to Redwood allowlist for a short window during migration. Thanks for the help! :tada:

andrew-eng: Nice — glad you got it. For future, recommend: enable Private DNS on creation, avoid host-level TLS interception for PrivateLink ENIs, and keep a small canary to validate AZs before full rollout. I'll paste a short RFC we use for endpoint hardening.

infra-bot: Note: ticket #CS-2026 escalated -> resolved. Labels: privatelink, dns, tls, egress.

marta-support: Closing here; reopen if anything else crops up.
